memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So the Lord gave Israel all the land he had sworn to give their ancestors, and they took possession of it and settled there. The Lord gave them rest on every side, just as he had sworn to their ancestors. Not one of their enemies withstood them; the Lord gave all their enemies into their hands. Not one of all the Lord's good promises to Israel failed; every one was fulfilled. — Josh 21:43-45 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is one of the great summary verses of the whole Bible: "Not one of all the Lord's good promises to Israel failed; every one was fulfilled." After all the battles, the waiting, the wandering and the doubts, this is the verdict. God kept every word.

Think of how long Israel had waited. The promise to Abraham was centuries old. There had been slavery in Egypt, forty years in the wilderness, and years of war in Canaan. At many points it must have seemed the promise would never come. Yet here they are, settled in the land, with rest on every side. God's timing was not our timing, but His word did not fail.

This does not mean Israel's story was now perfect — the very next chapters show new struggles. But it does mean that God is utterly reliable. His good promises do not fall to the ground.

For us, this points straight to Christ. Every promise God has made about salvation, forgiveness, and eternal rest is guaranteed in Him. The rest Israel found in the land was only a shadow of the deeper rest we find in Jesus (Heb 4:8-10). If not one of God's good words failed for Israel, not one will fail for you. Rest today on the God who always keeps His word.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there a promise of God you are still waiting to see fulfilled?
2. How does Israel's story build your confidence in God's faithfulness?
3. Have you found your rest in Christ, the fulfilment of every promise?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Faithful God, not one of Your good promises has ever failed. Thank You for the rest I find in Jesus. Help me to trust You even while I wait, knowing Your word never falls to the ground. Amen.
